content: 1. The study published in the European Journal of Clinical Pharmacology in 2009 (Volume 65, Issue 9, Pages 935–940) discusses a health economic evaluation. 2. Personne M and Persson H conducted an independent study in Sweden to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of a poison center. This was presented in the abstracts of the European Association of Poison Centres and Clinical Toxicologists XXII International Congress, published in the Journal of Toxicology Clinical Toxicology in 2002 (Volume 40, Issue 3, Page 294). 3. Elamin MEMO, James DA, Holmes P, Jackson G, Thompson JP, Sandilands EA, and colleagues reported reductions in emergency department visits following the use of the UK National Poisons Information Service by primary healthcare providers. This study was published in Clinical Toxicology (Philadelphia) in 2018 (Volume 56, Issue 5, Pages 342–347). 4. Ponampalam R and Loh C analyzed the cost benefits of the Drug and Poison Information Centre in Singapore, particularly in preventing unnecessary hospitalizations. Their findings were published in the Hong Kong Journal of Emergency Medicine in 2010 (Volume 17, Issue 1, Pages 45–53). 5. Huynh A, Cairns R, Brown JA, Jan S, Robinson J, Lynch AM, and colleagues demonstrated healthcare cost savings achieved through advice provided by the Australian Poisons Information Centre for low-risk exposure calls. This was part of the SNAPSHOT 2 study, published in Clinical Toxicology (Philadelphia) in 2019 (Volume 57). 6. West J, Taylor L, Smith N, and Yu J highlighted cost savings achieved through community access to the New South Wales Poisons Information Centre. Their findings were published in the Australian Health Review in 1987 (Volume 10, Issue 3, Pages 238–247). 7. Annex 2 of the document lists resources on toxicology and general medicine identified by members of the WHO expert group as useful for poison centers. The inclusion of these resources does not imply endorsement by the World Health Organization. It is recommended that poison centers or accessible libraries maintain up-to-date textbooks on pediatrics, nephrology, hepatology, pulmonary disease, gastroenterology, cardiology, ophthalmology, gynecology, obstetrics, dermatology, and psychiatry. 8. The listed medical and general toxicology resources include: General and Applied Toxicology (3rd edition, 2009) edited by Ballantyne B, Marrs T, and Syversen T. Oxford Desk Reference: Toxicology (2014) edited by Bateman DN, Jefferson RD, Thomas SHL, Thompson JP, and Vale JA. Patty’s Toxicology (6th edition, 2012) edited by Bingham E and Cohrssen B. Critical Care Toxicology (2nd edition, 2017) published by Springer International Publishing. The 5-Minute Toxicology Consult (2000) edited by Dart RC. Management of Poisoning (3rd edition, 2007) by Fernando R. Illustrated Toxicology (2018) by Gupta PK. Casarett and Doull’s Toxicology: The Basic Science of Poisons (9th edition, 2019) edited by Klaassen CD. Toxicology Handbook (3rd edition, 2015) by Murray L, Little M, Pascu O, and Hoggett KA. Goldfrank’s Toxicologic Emergencies (11th edition, 2019) edited by Nelson LS, Howland MA, Lewin NA, Smith SW, Goldfrank LR, and Hoffman RS. Poisoning and Drug Overdose (7th edition, 2017) published by McGraw-Hill Education. Fundamentals of Toxicology (4th edition, 2011) by Pandey K, Shukla JP, and Trivedi SP. Modern Medical Toxicology (4th edition, 2013) by Pillay VV. Comprehensive Medical Toxicology (3rd edition, 2018) by Pillay VV. 9. Additional resources in French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish are also listed, covering clinical toxicology, occupational toxicology, analytical toxicology, natural toxins, and chemical warfare. 10. The document emphasizes the importance of acquiring books on natural toxins based on the geographical risks of poisoning by animals or plants. Illustrated guides with drawings, photographs, or specimens are particularly useful for identifying local flora and fauna. 11. Specific examples of literature on natural toxins include: Medical Toxicology of Natural Substances (2008) edited by Barceloux DG. Poisonous Plants and Fungi: An Illustrated Guide (2nd edition, 2003) edited by Cooper MR, Johnson AW, and Dauncey EA. Handbook of Poisonous and Injurious Plants (2nd edition, 2007) edited by Nelson LS, Shih RD, and Balick MJ. 12. The document also provides guidelines for managing snakebites and venomous animal injuries, with references to global and regional resources.
